content: Immunostimulators are substances, including drugs and nutrients, that enhance the immune system by either activating it or increasing the activity of its components. A prominent example of an immunostimulator is granulocyte-macrophage colony-stimulating factor, which is commercially available under the brand name Leukine. Additionally, the plant Echinacea has been attributed with certain immunostimulating properties. Immunostimulators can be classified into two primary categories: 1. Specific immunostimulators: These are agents that elicit an immune response with antigenic specificity. Examples include vaccines or any substance that acts as an antigen to provoke a targeted immune reaction. 2. Non-specific immunostimulators: These agents enhance the immune response without regard to antigenic specificity. They may amplify the immune response to various antigens or stimulate components of the immune system in a non-specific manner. Examples include adjuvants and other non-specific immunostimulating agents.
